WITH per_year AS (
  SELECT year,
         AVG(orbital_period) AS overall_mean_orbital_period,
         AVG(mass) AS overall_mean_mass,
         AVG(distance) AS overall_mean_distance,
         COUNT(*) AS total_count
  FROM planets
  GROUP BY year
),
per_year_method AS (
  SELECT year,
         method,
         AVG(orbital_period) AS method_mean_orbital_period,
         AVG(mass) AS method_mean_mass,
         AVG(distance) AS method_mean_distance,
         COUNT(*) AS method_count
  FROM planets
  GROUP BY year, method
),
weighted AS (
  SELECT pm.year,
         SUM(pm.method_mean_orbital_period * pm.method_count / py.total_count) AS weighted_mean_orbital_period,
         SUM(pm.method_mean_mass * pm.method_count / py.total_count) AS weighted_mean_mass,
         SUM(pm.method_mean_distance * pm.method_count / py.total_count) AS weighted_mean_distance
  FROM per_year_method pm
  JOIN per_year py ON pm.year = py.year
  GROUP BY pm.year
)
SELECT py.year,
       py.overall_mean_orbital_period,
       py.overall_mean_mass,
       py.overall_mean_distance,
       w.weighted_mean_orbital_period,
       w.weighted_mean_mass,
       w.weighted_mean_distance,
       py.overall_mean_orbital_period - w.weighted_mean_orbital_period AS diff_orbital_period,
       py.overall_mean_mass - w.weighted_mean_mass AS diff_mass,
       py.overall_mean_distance - w.weighted_mean_distance AS diff_distance
FROM per_year py
JOIN weighted w ON py.year = w.year
ORDER BY py.year;

instruction:
Using the `planets` table, produce a CSV with the following columns:
- `year`
- `overall_mean_orbital_period` (AVG of orbital_period, ignoring NULLs)
- `overall_mean_mass` (AVG of mass, ignoring NULLs)
- `overall_mean_distance` (AVG of distance, ignoring NULLs)
- `weighted_mean_orbital_period` (sum over methods of method_mean_orbital_period * method_fraction, where method_fraction = COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE method = m) / COUNT(*) for that year)
- `weighted_mean_mass` (same weighted sum for mass, ignoring NULLs)
- `weighted_mean_distance` (same weighted sum for distance, ignoring NULLs)
- `diff_orbital_period` = overall_mean_orbital_period - weighted_mean_orbital_period
- `diff_mass` = overall_mean_mass - weighted_mean_mass
- `diff_distance` = overall_mean_distance - weighted_mean_distance

Compute the weighted means using the method‑level means and the method fractions per year. Return only the CSV with a header row and one row per year, ordered by `year` ascending. Do not include any other output.

message:
WITH method_counts AS (
  SELECT number, method, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM planets
  GROUP BY number, method
), total_counts AS (
  SELECT number, COUNT(*) AS total
  FROM planets
  GROUP BY number
), method_percent AS (
  SELECT mc.number, mc.method, mc.cnt, ROUND(100.0 * mc.cnt / tc.total, 2) AS percent
  FROM method_counts mc JOIN total_counts tc USING (number)
), orbital_stats AS (
  SELECT number,
    ROUND(AVG(orbital_period),2) AS mean,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY orbital_period),2) AS median,
    ROUND(STDDEV_POP(orbital_period),2) AS std,
    ROUND(MIN(orbital_period),2) AS min,
    ROUND(MAX(orbital_period),2) AS max
  FROM planets
  WHERE orbital_period IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY number
), mass_stats AS (
  SELECT number,
    ROUND(AVG(mass),2) AS mean,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY mass),2) AS median,
    ROUND(STDDEV_POP(mass),2) AS std,
    ROUND(MIN(mass),2) AS min,
    ROUND(MAX(mass),2) AS max,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN mass IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*),2) AS missing_percent
  FROM planets
  GROUP BY number
)
SELECT number,

WITH stats AS (
  SELECT
    AVG(number) AS mean_number,
    AVG(orbital_period) AS mean_orbital,
    AVG(mass) AS mean_mass
  FROM planets
  WHERE orbital_period IS NOT NULL
), cov AS (
  SELECT
    SUM((number - s.mean_number) * (orbital_period - s.mean_orbital)) AS cov_num_orb,
    SUM((number - s.mean_number) * (mass - s.mean_mass)) AS cov_num_mass
  FROM planets p, stats s
  WHERE orbital_period IS NOT NULL AND mass IS NOT NULL
), var AS (
  SELECT
    SUM((number - s.mean_number) * (number - s.mean_number)) AS var_number,
    SUM((orbital_period - s.mean_orbital) * (orbital_period - s.mean_orbital)) AS var_orbital,
    SUM((mass - s.mean_mass) * (mass - s.mean_mass)) AS var_mass
  FROM planets p, stats s
  WHERE orbital_period IS NOT NULL AND mass IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  ROUND(cov.cov_num_orb / SQRT(var.var_number * var.var_orbital), 2) AS number_orbital_period,
  ROUND(cov.cov_num_mass / SQRT(var.var_number * var.var_mass), 2) AS number_mass
FROM cov, var;

- `mean_mass`, `median_mass`, `stddev_mass` (ignore NULLs)
- `mean_distance`, `median_distance`, `stddev_distance` (ignore NULLs)
- `percent_of_year` = 100.0 * count / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM planets WHERE year = outer.year)
Order the results by `year` ascending, then `method`. Return only the CSV with a header row and one row per year‑method combination.

message: The analysis shows that the Transit method dominates the 2010 discoveries, making up more than 70 % of that year’s planets, while Radial Velocity remains the most common method in 2009. Median orbital periods are very short for Transit planets (≈1–2 days) but spread more widely for Radial‑Velocity planets. SELECT method,
       COUNT(*) AS count,
       CORR(year, orbital_period) OVER (PARTITION BY method) AS corr_year_orbital_period,
       CORR(year, mass) OVER (PARTITION BY method) AS corr_year_mass,
       CORR(year, distance) OVER (PARTITION BY method) AS corr_year_distance
FROM planets
GROUP BY method
ORDER BY method;

instruction:
Using the `planets` table, produce a single JSON object with the following keys:

1. `overall_method_distribution`: array of `{method, count, percent}` for all records.
2. `method_stats`: array of `{method, mean_orbital_period, mean_mass, multi_system_percent, mean_orbital_period_single, mean_orbital_period_multi, mean_mass_single, mean_mass_multi, missing_mass_percent_single, missing_mass_percent_multi}`. Compute:
   - `multi_system_percent` = proportion of planets detected by that method that belong to systems with `number > 1`.
   - `mean_orbital_period_single` / `mean_orbital_period_multi` = mean orbital period for planets of that method in single‑planet vs multi‑planet systems (exclude NULL periods).
   - `mean_mass_single` / `mean_mass_multi` = mean mass for planets of that method in single‑planet vs multi‑planet systems (exclude NULL masses).
   - `missing_mass_percent_single` / `missing_mass_percent_multi` = proportion of planets of that method in single‑planet vs multi‑planet systems with NULL mass.
3. `by_number`: array of objects, one per distinct `number` value, each containing:
   - `number`
   - `total`
   - `method_counts`: array of `{method, count, percent}` for that number
   - `orbital_period_stats`: `{mean, median, std, min, max}` (exclude NULLs)
   - `mass_stats`: `{mean, median, std, min, max, missing_percent}` (exclude NULLs for stats, compute missing_percent as proportion of rows with NULL mass)
4. `correlations`: `{number_orbital_period: pearson, number_mass: pearson}` – compute Pearson correlation between `number` and `orbital_period` (exclude NULLs) and between `number` and `mass` (exclude NULLs).
5. `single_vs_multi`: object with two sub‑objects `single` and `multi`, each containing:
   - `count`
   - `mean_orbital_period`
   - `mean_mass` (exclude NULLs)

Round all numeric values to two decimal places. Percent columns must sum to 100 % within each group (allowing for rounding). Return only the JSON object, no explanatory text or SQL queries. Use standard SQL aggregate functions; you may need sub‑queries or CTEs to compute the percent columns.

message: From 1989 to 2014 the exoplanet catalog shifted from a radial‑velocity‑dominated, short‑period, high‑mass sample to a transit‑rich population of longer‑period, lower‑mass planets. Mean orbital period climbed by roughly 140 days per year (≈+0.15 Pearson correlation), mean mass fell by about 0.13 M⊕ per year, and mean distance grew by ~18 pc per year, reflecting the growing reach of transit surveys. Transit detections, which rose from <10 % to >70 % of yearly discoveries, drive the longer periods and lighter planets, while radial‑velocity planets—still ~90 % of all detections—cluster at shorter periods and higher masses. Notable outliers include the 2006 Imaging group, whose single long‑period planet inflated the mean to 26,762 days and stddev to 135,342 days, and the 2011 surge of 185 planets (94 RV) that temporarily inflated yearly counts. The analysis is limited by 50 % missing mass values, 22 % missing distances, and small sub‑groups for rare methods, so correlations and averages should be interpreted with caution.

message:
WITH stats AS (
SELECT method,
SUM(CASE WHEN number>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS multi_count,
COUNT(*) AS total_count,
SUM(CASE WHEN number=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_single,
SUM(CASE WHEN number>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_multi,
AVG(CASE WHEN number=1 AND orbital_period IS NOT NULL THEN orbital_period END) AS mean_orbital_period_single,
AVG(CASE WHEN number>1 AND orbital_period IS NOT NULL THEN orbital_period END) AS mean_orbital_period_multi,
AVG(CASE WHEN number=1 AND mass IS NOT NULL THEN mass END) AS mean_mass_single,
AVG(CASE WHEN number>1 AND mass IS NOT NULL THEN mass END) AS mean_mass_multi,
SUM(CASE WHEN number=1 AND mass IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS missing_mass_single,
SUM(CASE WHEN number>1 AND mass IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS missing_mass_multi
FROM planets
GROUP BY method
)
SELECT method,
ROUND(100.0*multi_count/total_count,2) AS multi_system_percent,
ROUND(mean_orbital_period_single,2) AS mean_orbital_period_single,
ROUND(mean_orbital_period_multi,2) AS mean_orbital_period_multi,
ROUND(mean_mass_single,2) AS mean_mass_single,
ROUND(mean_mass_multi,2) AS mean_mass_multi,
ROUND(100.0*missing_mass_single/NULLIF(count_single,0),2) AS missing_mass_percent_single,
ROUND(100.0*missing_mass_multi/NULLIF(count_multi,0),2) AS missing_mass_percent_multi
FROM stats;

SUM(CASE WHEN number>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS multi_count,
COUNT(*) AS total_count,
SUM(CASE WHEN number=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_single,
SUM(CASE WHEN number>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_multi,

AVG(CASE WHEN number>1 AND orbital_period IS NOT NULL THEN orbital_period END) AS mean_orbital_period_multi,
AVG(CASE WHEN number=1 AND mass IS NOT NULL THEN mass END) AS mean_mass_single,
AVG(CASE WHEN number>1 AND mass IS NOT NULL THEN mass END) AS mean_mass_multi,
SUM(CASE WHEN number=1 AND mass IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS missing_mass_single,
SUM(CASE WHEN number>1 AND mass IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS missing_mass_multi
FROM planets
GROUP BY method

method_dist AS (
  SELECT method,
         COUNT(*) AS count,
         ROUND(100.0*COUNT(*)/total.total,2) AS percent
  FROM planets CROSS JOIN total
  GROUP BY method
),
method_stats AS (
  SELECT method,

         ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN mass IS NOT NULL THEN mass END),2) AS mean_mass,
         ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN number>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS multi_system_percent,
         ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN number=1 AND orbital_period IS NOT NULL THEN orbital_period END),2) AS mean_orbital_period_single,
         ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN number>1 AND orbital_period IS NOT NULL THEN orbital_period END),2) AS mean_orbital_period_multi,
         ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN number=1 AND mass IS NOT NULL THEN mass END),2) AS mean_mass_single,
         ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN number>1 AND mass IS NOT NULL THEN mass END),2) AS mean_mass_multi,
         ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN number=1 AND mass IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN number=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS missing_mass_percent_single,
         ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN number>1 AND mass IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN number>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS missing_mass_percent_multi
  FROM planets
  GROUP BY method
),
by_number AS (
  SELECT number,
         COUNT(*) AS total,

Radial Velocity dominates detections (53.43 %) and shows a moderate multi‑system fraction (40.69 %). Transit detections, while fewer, have a very high missing‑mass rate (≈99 %). Correlations are weak and negative: number of planets is slightly inversely related to both orbital period (‑0.06) and mass (‑0.24). Missing mass is most common in single‑planet systems, especially for Transit and Imaging methods. All statistics exclude NULLs where appropriate and percentages are rounded to two decimals.
